intro: A few questions to help the lesson settle. Nothing here is scored or seen by anyone but you, and you may leave any of them blank.

questions.prompt: Psalm 94:19 — "When the cares of my heart are many, your ______ cheer my soul."
In Psalm 94:19 the writer is describing a mind that has become calm.
questions.note: The cares are still many. God's comfort reaches him in the middle of them, not after they stop.

questions.prompt: What is the one question this lesson asks you to put to a thought that keeps running?
questions.answer: Where is this thought taking me?

questions.prompt: Thinking itself is the problem this lesson is trying to solve.
questions.note: Thinking is not the enemy. Good thinking goes somewhere and then stops.

questions.prompt: Good thinking leads to understanding, to a decision, or to what third thing?
Grace's difficulty was that her faith was weak.
questions.note: Her problem was not weak faith. It was a mind that had learnt to run without a destination.

questions.prompt: Useful thinking has a stopping point. What does mental circling often go looking for instead?
Where does your own mind most often circle — the future, another person's thoughts, or an outcome you cannot control?
Name one matter your mind keeps returning to. One sentence. You are not solving it here.
The lesson says a crowded mind is not proof of weak faith. Is that hard for you to believe? You may say so plainly.
